label: Bookings included in Voi Pass
scope: The upgrade incentive scales with the share of bookings the Pass covers; every included booking still costs a placement. Pass holders respond to the average fee they pay per booking (nothing within the allowance). The Pass price is a calibration input, so the allowance is not a priced tier. Under the linear response, a booking that costs a Pass holder nothing doubles their reference adoption (fee 0 is a 100% cut from the 25 kr anchor), so allowances beyond about 2 a month lie outside the response’s local range.

label: Booking fee (incl. VAT)
scope: Set at 35 kr: at 25 kr a booking costs more to place and hold than it earns. The adoption inputs describe demand at the 25 kr reference fee; at 35 kr the default price response (elasticity 1) lowers adoption by 40%. The price table under Stress Test shows other responses. Benchmarks: Voi’s free-unlock add-on 29 kr a month; Dott and Lime offer 10–15 minute holds free (non-Oslo analogues: the Oslo permits are held by Voi, Ryde and Bolt).

label: Demand response to the fee
scope: Unestimated planning coefficient. Default 1; sensitivity range 0–2 is a scenario range, not an empirical confidence interval.

label: Use bounded logit price response
scope: Alternative unestimated demand structure. Linear and logit share adoption at the reference fee and the same local price elasticity there. Logit(p) = logit(p0) − elasticity × (fee − reference) / reference / (1 − p0), for 0 < p0 < 1. Price-response envelopes and the assumption challenge test both forms. Train (2009), chapter 3, motivates the probability form, not its Voi parameter values.
